Integrate a split-potential Hamiltonian (multiple time-stepping)

Source: R/integrate.R
simp_integrate_mts.Rd

Advance a separable Hamiltonian whose potential splits as U = U_slow + U_fast, using the RESPA / Verlet-I multiple-time-stepping integrator. The slow force is evaluated once per outer step while the fast force drives m inner leapfrog substeps, so a stiff-but-cheap part (a Gaussian latent prior, say) can take the small steps it needs without paying for the expensive-but-smooth part (a likelihood) at the same rate. The step is symmetric, time reversible, and symplectic.

Usage

simp_integrate_mts(
  q0,
  p0,
  grad_slow,
  grad_fast,
  eps,
  n_steps,
  m,
  mass = NULL,
  trajectory = FALSE,
  U = NULL
)

Arguments

q0

Numeric vector, the starting position.

p0

Numeric vector, the starting momentum, same length as q0.

grad_slow, grad_fast

Functions mapping a position to the gradient of the slow and fast potential parts. Their sum is dU/dq.

eps

Positive outer step size.

n_steps

Number of outer steps.

m

Number of inner fast substeps per outer step.

mass

Mass matrix M, as in simp_integrate().

trajectory

If TRUE, return the position and momentum at every outer step. If FALSE (the default), return only the endpoint.

U

Optional function mapping a position to the total potential energy U_slow + U_fast. When supplied, the total energy is recorded along the returned points.

Value

A list with the endpoint q and p, and, when requested, q_path, p_path, and energy, as in simp_integrate().

Examples

# Stiff Gaussian prior (fast) plus a soft quadratic likelihood (slow).
grad_fast <- function(q) 100 * q
grad_slow <- function(q) 0.1 * q
out <- simp_integrate_mts(q0 = c(1, 0), p0 = c(0, 1),
                          grad_slow = grad_slow, grad_fast = grad_fast,
                          eps = 0.2, n_steps = 30, m = 10)
out$q
